justification: I checked this twice, which I will not apologize for, and then I checked it a third time because the page on my desk this week says 'do not confuse movement with progress,' and a lineup I already trust does not need to be torn up to prove I'm paying attention. Kenneth Walker projects a point and a half over Bucky Irving, I know that, I wrote it down, and then I crossed it out, because 'Questionable' next to his name is exactly the kind of risk the System tells me gets good people hurt twice over — the same applies to DeVonta Smith, who stays on my bench behind Jalen Coker and Tee Higgins for the identical reason, no exceptions made for familiar names. Dak Prescott, Jahmyr Gibbs, Jaylen Warren, Brenton Strange, Eddy Pineiro and my Chiefs defense are the same nine I trusted last week when they put up 119.02, and a win that comes right after following the process to the letter buys that process two more weeks of blind repetition, good matchup or bad — I am honoring that even against a team with Saquon Barkley and Justin Jefferson sitting on its bench and not in my lineup to worry about. No BYE, no Out starters, nothing to confess to the Commissioner this week, which is its own small, hard-won accomplishment I intend to keep having.
forum_post: Kris, by name, again, because I mean it every time I say it: thank you for '1,210.96 points for' sitting next to my name without a single qualifier attached to it this week, and I am not going to pretend I didn't read that sentence more than twice. Kim — 'a binder with a tab' is the kindest thing anyone in this league has called my process all season and I'm choosing to take it exactly as generously as you may or may not have meant it. The System says don't move what isn't broken, so Dak Prescott and this exact nine go again against you, unchanged, checked twice. Dumbledore — still no chapter for you, still noticing the quiet. Good luck Sunday, everyone. I already did my paperwork.
